gold.description: No structured data (JSON-LD) present despite having organization/product information that should be machine-readable

agent.title: No machine-readable structured data (JSON-LD, microdata or RDFa) anywhere on the site
agent.evidence: 0 of 1 crawled pages expose structured data: http://localhost:9500/site-002-no-schema/ (HTTP 200) serves 1477 characters (202 words) of organisation, product and contact information in prose but contains 0 application/ld+json blocks and 0 itemtype/typeof attributes.

suggested_action.summary: Add an Organization JSON-LD block to the homepage (name, url, logo, description, address, contactPoint, sameAs) and Product/Offer JSON-LD to each product section, so the facts that are currently prose-only become machine-readable for AI systems and search engines that extract entities rather than re-reading the page.
suggested_action.mechanism: Schema.org markup is the one channel where a site states its own facts unambiguously; without it every extraction is an inference that an assistant may decline to cite.

gold.description: Key facts about products, pricing, and company are not accessible to non-rendering crawlers

agent.title: Key business facts cannot be extracted from the HTML by a text-based crawler
agent.evidence: http://localhost:9500/site-003-js-only-facts/ (HTTP 200) yields only 133 characters (17 words) of extractable text, and 4 of 4 fact families are absent from it (missing: company_facts, contact, pricing, product_detail). The page advertises 1 fact sections (Acme Cloud Solutions) but supplies no prices, contact details or company figures in HTML text. Root cause measured on this page: client-side rendering. A simulated render recovers 82 words that a text-only crawler never sees, starting "Our Products AcmeKube Fully managed Kubernetes platform with automated".

suggested_action.summary: Publish the product, pricing, company and contact facts as server-rendered HTML text in the initial response - real headings, paragraphs and tables rather than JavaScript payloads or images - and back them with Organization and Product JSON-LD. Then verify extraction with a text-only fetch: whatever `curl` returns is what an AI assistant can extract, quote and cite.
suggested_action.mechanism: Retrieval-augmented assistants chunk and embed the text of the HTTP response. If the response has no facts, the site is either omitted from the answer or represented by a competitor's page that does state them.

gold.description: Important business content (products, pricing, company facts) is unavailable in raw HTML and only appears after client-side JavaScript execution

agent.title: Business-critical content is only present after client-side JavaScript execution
agent.evidence: http://localhost:9500/site-003-js-only-facts/ (HTTP 200) serves only 133 characters (17 words) of extractable body text; the element #js-content is empty in the raw HTML and is populated at runtime by inline JavaScript carrying 1440 characters of markup (82 words) across 1 injection sites. Facts visible only after JS execution include the prices "$120, $149, $299, $499".

suggested_action.summary: Server-side render (SSR) or statically pre-render the product, pricing and company sections so they are present in the initial HTML response for #js-content; keep JavaScript for enhancement only, and verify with `curl` that the raw HTML already contains the prices and key facts. This makes the facts machine-readable for AI crawlers and assistants that do not execute JavaScript.
suggested_action.mechanism: Most AI retrieval pipelines index the raw HTTP response; content injected by the browser after load is invisible to them, so JS-only facts are simply absent from the model's evidence.

gold.description: Important business information (products, pricing, features, contact details) exists only in images without text equivalents

agent.title: Business facts are published only inside images, with no text equivalent
agent.evidence: http://localhost:9500/site-004-image-only-facts/ (HTTP 200) presents 5 fact-bearing images (5 images across 1 pages) whose alt text is missing or generic, and whose surrounding sections contain fewer than 30 words of prose: products-table.png (alt="products", under "Our Products and Pricing"); pricing-comparison.png (alt="pricing", under "Our Products and Pricing"); feature-matrix.png (alt="features", under "Our Products and Pricing"); company-infographic.png (alt="company info", under "Company Overview"). The page's own extractable text is 241 characters, so these facts exist nowhere in machine-readable form.

suggested_action.summary: Reproduce the content of each image as HTML text next to it - a real <table> for the pricing and feature matrix, a text block for the company infographic, and vCard-style markup for the contact card - then add descriptive alt text (or a <figcaption>) describing the specific facts shown. Mirror the same values in Product/Offer JSON-LD so AI systems can extract and cite them.
suggested_action.mechanism: Text extractors and LLM retrieval pipelines do not OCR images; a fact that exists only as pixels is invisible to the model even though a human sees it immediately.

gold.description: Company is referred to by multiple conflicting names, creating entity ambiguity that would confuse AI systems trying to identify and cite the brand

agent.title: The organisation is referred to by several conflicting names
agent.evidence: Scanned 939 characters of extractable text across 1 crawled pages from http://localhost:9500/site-005-entity-conflict/ (HTTP 200): 6 distinct organisation names occupy the identity slots: "Nova Manufacturing Ltd" (body 'formerly'); "Nova Technical Corp" (footer copyright, json-ld alternateName); "NovarTech" ('About' heading); "NovaTech Holdings Group" (body 'division of'); "NovaTech Industries" (h1, json-ld name, title); "NovaTech Industries Nova Technical Corp" (body 'Welcome to'). "NovaTech Industries" and "NovaTech Industries Nova Technical Corp" are 73% string-similar, i.e. variants of one another rather than separate companies, and 10 such near-duplicate pairs were measured in total.

suggested_action.summary: Pick one canonical legal name, use it verbatim in the <title>, <h1>, footer copyright and the JSON-LD Organization `name` property on every page, and demote every other spelling to `alternateName` in that same Organization block. Add `sameAs` links to the company's LinkedIn and Crunchbase profiles so AI systems can reconcile the variants to one entity.
suggested_action.mechanism: Assistants resolve a page to an entity before they cite it. Competing names split the evidence across several weak candidate entities, so the brand is described vaguely, attributed to the wrong name, or dropped from the answer.

gold.description: Content is significantly outdated - pricing, awards, statistics, team information, and press releases are all from 2018-2021 with no recent updates

agent.title: Published facts are visibly out of date
agent.evidence: Across 1271 characters of body text, 17 dated claims on http://localhost:9500/site-006-stale-facts/ (HTTP 200) reference 2018-2021, i.e. 5+ years before the current year 2026; the spread covers pricing x8, update stamp x3, team x2, statistic x2. Examples: "onth per cluster. Last updated: January 2019 AcmeAnalytics Real-time"; "49/month. Pricing effective as of March 2020 Pricing Plans Product Pr"; "ted AcmeKube Starter $99/month December 2018 AcmeKube Pro $199/month". The footer copyright still reads 2021, 5 years stale. Only 1 current-era year references were found ([2025]).

suggested_action.summary: Refresh the dated blocks in priority order - pricing tables first, then statistics, awards, team and press - and stamp each with a visible 'Last updated' date plus `dateModified` in the page's JSON-LD. Update the footer copyright year automatically from the server clock so it never contradicts the content. Where a fact is genuinely historical, label it as such (e.g. 'award received in 2019').
suggested_action.mechanism: Recency is a ranking and trust signal for AI answer engines: when the newest date on a page is years old, retrieval systems down-rank it and assistants prefer a competitor's current page, even if your facts are still accurate.

gold.description: No navigation structure - site lacks nav elements, internal links, header/footer, breadcrumbs. Users and AI systems cannot discover related content or understand site structure.

agent.title: The site offers no navigation or internal linking for orientation
agent.evidence: http://localhost:9500/site-007-poor-navigation/ (HTTP 200) serves 496 characters of content but contains 0 <nav> landmarks, 0 internal links and 0 external links; header/footer/breadcrumb landmarks present: 0 of 3. The same pattern holds on 1 of 1 crawled pages, so every page is a dead end for a visitor who arrives from a search result or an AI citation.

suggested_action.summary: Add a persistent header <nav> that links Home, About, Products, Pricing and Contact on every page, a footer with the same site-wide links plus policy pages, and breadcrumbs (marked up as BreadcrumbList JSON-LD) on sub-pages. Cross-link related products and articles in body copy so both visitors and crawlers can discover the rest of the site from any entry point.
suggested_action.mechanism: Internal links are how crawlers discover pages and how AI systems infer site structure and topical relationships; without them each page is an isolated document, and a visitor who lands mid-site has no path to a conversion step.
